subject: Fjord-0.7b elevated 5xx/timeouts — incident notification and next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Riley Chan <riley@fjordanalytics.com>, infra@fjordanalytics.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fjord-0.7b — elevated 5xx/timeouts impacting your gen endpoints (temporary mitigation)

Hi Riley / Fjord infra team,

Quick heads-up: since ~08:50 UTC we’ve observed an increase in 5xx responses and generation timeouts for requests routed to model "Fjord-0.7b" for your account (project: fjord-analytics-prod). We are seeing elevated token-generation latency and a correlated rise in transient 5xx (502/504) across shorter-sequence text-generation calls.

What we’ve done so far:
- Scoped the impact: ~3.2% of requests to your model footprint (spike window 08:50–09:05 UTC). Attached are sample error traces and a short SLO impact chart.
- Rerouted a fraction of traffic to a compatible variant (fjord-0.7b-v2-small) while retaining session affinity for active chats.
- Rolled back a runtime tweak that was staged at 08:30 UTC (safe rollback completed at 09:05 UTC).

Immediate ask from you: could you confirm whether you have any in-flight canary traffic or scheduled batch jobs hitting the same endpoints? If so, we’ll prioritize those sessions for graceful failover.

Planned next steps (internal): Ben, Priyom, and the runtime team are triaging kernel selection logs and cache eviction metrics. We’ll follow up with a full update and a mitigation timeline within the hour.

We’re sorry for the disruption — I’ll keep you posted with concrete ETA for full remediation and a proposed credit if the incident materially affected SLAs.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fjord-0.7b elevated 5xx — triage notes and immediate remediation actions

Short triage notes:
- Symptom: transient 5xx and generation timeouts correlated with a spike in small-sequence requests (< 64 tokens) against Fjord-0.7b. Error patterns show failed kernel selection and repeated KV-cache misses leading to excessive recompute.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): a recent optimization (PR #8342) that modified aggressive KV cache eviction thresholds under memory pressure caused cache churn for models with many short-history calls. This triggered excess kernel recompilation / OOM retries in the serving runtime for certain quantized paths.

Mitigation taken (completed):
1) Rolled back PR #8342 on the serving fleet at 09:05 UTC.
2) Activated traffic-level fallback to fjord-0.7b-v2-small for the affected routing policy.
3) Temporarily increased per-worker memory headroom and disabled an experimental kernel-prefetch in the 0.7b quant path.

Outstanding actions (owners + ETA):
- Priyom: produce a rollback verification run and a controlled canary to validate stability across 2 hours (ETA 11:30 UTC).
- Olga: collect a full set of kernel logs and client-side retry traces for egress analysis (ETA 10:30 UTC).
- Jonas: prepare a postmortem draft and remediation timeline (ETA EOD today).

Customer comms: Tessa to confirm current customer impact, proposed credit and schedule a 30-min post-incident sync tomorrow to review the postmortem.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft-0829.md (work-in-progress)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Riley Chan <riley@fjordanalytics.com>, infra@fjordanalytics.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident update: Fjord-0.7b — remediation complete, postmortem and credits

Hi Riley — follow-up after our triage: 

Status and resolution summary
- Root cause: aggressive KV-cache eviction thresholds introduced in PR #8342 caused cache churn under short-sequence workloads, leading to kernel-selection instability and transient 5xx/timeouts for the fjord-0.7b quantized path.
- Resolution: the runtime rollback and traffic fallback completed successfully; we observed error rates return to baseline by 10:45 UTC on 2028-08-29.
- Impact to you: we estimate ~3.2% of your gen requests during the spike window saw elevated failure/latency.

Next steps and remediation timeline
- Code fix: Priyom’s team will land a safe patch to adjust eviction thresholds and add a regression test for short-sequence workloads (target: 2028-09-05).
- Operational hardening: we’ll add a circuit-breaker that auto-fails over short-sequence traffic to the v2-small variant when cache thrashing is detected (ETA: 2028-09-12).

Credits and meeting
- We’ll apply a one-time credit for the affected window; Ben will follow up with a billing note and HubSpot entry.
- Would you be available for a 30-minute review tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the postmortem and verify the proposed mitigations? I’ve included a draft postmortem as an attachment and an internal drive link for details.

Apologies again for the disruption — we know reliability is critical and appreciate the fast coordination from your side. Please reply with a preferred meeting time if the suggested slot doesn’t work.

Best,
Tessa
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
